consensus_summary: The consensus primary reading treats 'works of the law' as deeds of obedience to the Mosaic law (Torah) relied upon for justification, which Paul rejects in contrast to faith; common alternatives include Jewish boundary markers, ceremonial prescriptions only, or generalized human merit/effort, with no settled consensus across traditions.
book_summary: Paul's phrase for deeds considered in relation to law; it is not a synonym for obedience and does not name one unchanging class of deeds. Context may identify God's law, a circumcision-party application, or leave the acts unnamed, but what is constant is denial that the deeds can purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt.
consensus_core_identification: Mosaic-law deeds used as the basis for justification (or related benefits), rejected by Paul.
book_core_identification: Context-determined deeds related to law, for which any purchase-price claim (justification, Spirit, standing, debt) is denied.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus primary (and many alternatives) fix or prioritize a relatively stable class of deeds (full Mosaic observance, boundary markers, or ceremonial subset); the book denies any unchanging class and lets the surrounding passage alone determine the particular acts.
rationale: Minimum cores both identify the phrase with law-related deeds whose power to justify (or produce the Spirit/standing) is denied. The book preserves that general category and the key Pauline rejection but materially refines precision and boundaries by rejecting synonymy with obedience or a fixed deed-class, making extension context-variable (covering circumcision-party cases among others). This is boundary/extension disagreement, not core replacement.
strongest_objection: The cited Pauline texts occur in tightly related Mosaic-law or Jewish-practice contexts, so the book's denial of any unchanging class may overstate variability and underplay textual consistency of the referent.
